# Settings catalogue: every setting, key and drone of ShramkoGSFPV

<!-- Generated by scripts/gen-catalog.ts from packages/prefs (the settings schema and the keymap), the drone presets and the simulator's dictionaries. Do not edit by hand: run `node --import tsx scripts/gen-catalog.ts`. -->

Everything you can change in [ShramkoGSFPV](https://gsfpv.flyreelstudio.eu), the open-source browser FPV drone simulator for 3D Gaussian Splatting scans: **68 settings in 11 groups, 34 keyboard keys, 9 drone presets and 5 rate-curve types**. Generated on 2026-10-17 from the simulator's own settings schema, so it lists only what ships today; a setting that is still being built appears here the day it ships. The same catalogue, in English, Spanish, Polish and Russian, is on the [landing page](https://gsfpv.flyreelstudio.eu/en/#tune).

- **Per drone:** each drone keeps its own value (camera, motor model, PID, rates…), so tuning one drone never changes another.
- **Per scene:** kept for each scan.
- **Drone preset:** the default is the drone's own number; shown here for the default drone, BetaFPV Pavo20 Pro class, 3S.

## Flight

| Setting | What it does | Default | Range or options | Scope | Key |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| **Flight mode**<br>`flight.mode` | Angle levels the drone when you let go of the sticks; Horizon levels it too but flips at full stick; Acro holds the attitude, like a freestyle quad. M or the mode chip switches it; a mode switch set on your radio's check screen decides instead. | Angle (self-levelling) | Acro (rate mode) · Angle (self-levelling) · Horizon (levels, flips allowed) | global | `M` |
| **Angle limit** (advanced)<br>`level.angleLimitDeg` | How far the drone tilts in angle mode at full stick: more tilt, more speed. Betaflight's angle_limit (60° by default). | 60° | 10–85° | per drone |  |
| **Angle strength** (advanced)<br>`level.strength` | How firmly angle mode levels the drone and follows the stick: higher is snappier. Betaflight's angle strength (angle_p_gain, 50 by default): at 100 the drone reaches half the stick's tilt in about 70 ms instead of 100. | 50 | 0–200 | per drone |  |
| **Horizon strength** (advanced)<br>`level.horizonStrength` | How firmly horizon mode levels the drone near the stick centre: higher levels harder. Betaflight's horizon level strength (75 by default). | 75 | 0–200 | per drone |  |

## Crashes & respawn

| Setting | What it does | Default | Range or options | Scope | Key |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| **Crashes**<br>`crash.enabled` | Off: hitting a wall only bounces the drone off, the motors keep spinning. On: a hard hit is a crash. | On |  | global |  |
| **Crash threshold**<br>`physics.vCrash` | Impact speed above which a hit counts as a crash; slower touches slide along the wall. | 4 m/s (drone preset) | 2–10 m/s | per drone |  |
| **Respawn after a crash**<br>`respawn.auto` | On: after a crash the drone comes back by itself, nothing to press. Off: the crash panel waits for you. | On |  | global |  |
| **Respawn delay**<br>`respawn.delayS` | How long the crash plays before the drone comes back. | 2 s | 0.5–10 s | global |  |
| **Respawn at**<br>`respawn.target` | A few seconds back along your path, or the start. | Back along the path | Back along the path · The start | global |  |
| **How far back**<br>`respawn.rewindS` | Seconds back along your path where the drone reappears: after a crash, when stuck, and with Y. | 5 s | 1–30 s | global |  |
| **Invisible platform**<br>`respawn.platform` | The drone appears on an invisible pad at that height and sits on it, motors on, until you lift off. | On |  | global |  |
| **Stay armed after a respawn**<br>`respawn.keepArmed` | With the arm switch still on, the drone is armed right after a respawn: no switch flip. | On |  | global |  |
| **Reset when stuck**<br>`respawn.unstuck` | Upside down or wedged and not moving: the drone goes a few seconds back by itself, like in Liftoff. | On |  | global |  |
| **Fresh battery**<br>`battery.refill` | When the pack is full again. | At the start (R, restart, new scene) | At the start (R, restart, new scene) · At every respawn · Never | global |  |

| Setting | What it does | Default | Range or options | Scope | Key |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| **Camera field of view**<br>`camera.fovDeg` | How wide the FPV camera sees. Each drone keeps its own value; a change never moves the drone. | 115° (drone preset) | 70–150° | per drone |  |

## Display

| Setting | What it does | Default | Range or options | Scope | Key |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| **Show HUD**<br>`display.hud` | The on-screen display: arm state, flight mode, battery, speed and altitude. H hides every text on the flight view for a moment. | On |  | global | `H` |
| **Stable frame ↔ detail** (advanced)<br>`display.quality` | Moves the render resolution and detail budget. Physics always runs at 1000 Hz. | 1 | 0–1 | global |  |
| **Drawing**<br>`display.drawing` | How the scan is drawn. Auto does what the scene's link asks (SuperSplat's ?stochastic and ?budget). Stochastic is SuperSplat's new drawing that skips sorting the splats and leaves a fine grain. Sorted is the classic, smooth drawing. Stochastic needs WebGPU in a desktop browser. | Auto (as the link asks) | Auto (as the link asks) · Stochastic (SuperSplat beta) · Sorted (classic) | global |  |
| **Reduced motion**<br>`display.reducedMotion` | A calmer crash camera without flashes; follows your system setting by default. | Follow the system | Follow the system · On · Off | global |  |
| **Frame stats**<br>`display.frameStats` | Screen refresh, frame times and input-to-screen delay over the flight view. F3 switches it. | Off |  | global | `F3` |
| **Language**<br>`ui.language` | English, Spanish, Polish or Russian; by default the language of the page. | Page language | Page language · English · Spanish · Polish · Russian | global |  |
| **Crosshair**<br>`crosshair.shape` | A mark in the centre of the view for lining up a gap. Off by default, like a real FPV feed. Never drawn into your videos, hidden in cinema mode. | Off | Off · Dot · Cross · Circle · Ring with a dot | global |  |
| **Crosshair size**<br>`crosshair.size` | As a share of the screen's shorter side, so it looks the same on a phone and on a big monitor. | 4 % | 1–20 % | global |  |
| **Crosshair colour**<br>`crosshair.color` | Pick one that stands out on the scan you fly. | Green | Green · White · Yellow · Red · Cyan · Magenta · Black | global |  |
| **Crosshair opacity**<br>`crosshair.opacity` | 1 is solid; lower lets the scan show through. | 0.8 | 0.1–1 | global |  |

|---|---|---|---|---|---|

## Controls

| Setting | What it does | Default | Range or options | Scope | Key |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| **Stick mode**<br>`input.stickMode` | Which stick is the throttle in the calibration drawings: Mode 2 on the left, Mode 1 on the right. | Mode 2 | Mode 1 · Mode 2 | global |  |
| **How touch and keyboard fly**<br>`input.play` | Easy play: no arming (the first stick or key starts the motors), the drone holds its height, keys like a game (W A S D move, arrows turn and climb), and a pilot school that takes the help away step by step. Pilot: as a radio — the ARM button or Space, a throttle that stays where you leave it, Mode 2 keys (W/S throttle, A/D yaw, arrows pitch and roll). A radio or a gamepad always flies as a radio. | Easy play | Easy play · Pilot (as a radio) | global |  |
| **Altitude help (easy play)**<br>`input.altitudeHelp` | The drone holds its height by itself; up and down (the arrows, or the left stick on a touch screen) climb and sink at a steady speed. Works in angle mode only: horizon and acro can flip, and there your throttle flies. Step 1 of the pilot school. | On |  | global |  |
| **Vibrate on a crash**<br>`input.haptics` | A short buzz when you crash with the touch sticks, on phones that allow it (most Android phones; not iPhone). | On |  | global |  |

## Drone & physics

| Setting | What it does | Default | Range or options | Scope | Key |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| **Drone**<br>`drone.current` | One of the presets: BetaFPV-class whoops, a 5-inch freestyle and a 5-inch race quad, an X8 cinelifter with a cinema camera; every number on its card says where it comes from. Each drone keeps its own settings. | BetaFPV Pavo20 Pro class, 3S | BetaFPV Pavo20 Pro class, 3S · BetaFPV Pavo20 Pro II class, 3S · BetaFPV Pavo20 Pro II class, 4S · BetaFPV Pavo Pico class, 2S · BetaFPV Meteor65 Pro class, 1S · BetaFPV Air65 Freestyle class, 1S · iFlight Nazgul Evoque F5 V3 class, 6S · iFlight Mach R5 Sport class, 6S · iFlight Taurus X8 class with a RED Komodo, 6S | global |  |
| **Camera load**<br>`drone.payload` | What the cinelifter carries under its frame. iFlight sells the Taurus X8 without a camera and allows up to 3 kg; the motors stay the same, so the weight, thrust-to-weight and hover throttle change with the camera. Chosen on the drone picker's 3D view; the other drones ignore it. | RED KOMODO 6K rig | RED KOMODO 6K rig · Blackmagic BMPCC 6K Pro rig · GoPro HERO13 Black · No camera | per drone |  |
| **Gravity**<br>`physics.gravity` | Earth 9.81, Moon 1.62, Mars 3.72, zero-g, or any value in between. | 9.81 m/s² | 0–30 m/s² | global |  |
| **Thrust on other worlds**<br>`physics.gravityMode` | Same motors (honest), the thrust-to-weight you have on Earth, or auto throttle that hovers at stick centre. | Real (same motors) | Real (same motors) · Keep thrust / weight · Auto throttle (stick centre hovers) | global |  |
| **Thrust-to-weight** (advanced)<br>`physics.twr` | Maximum thrust divided by weight; the preset takes it from the manufacturer or an estimate. | 5 (drone preset) | 2–16 | per drone |  |
| **Motor spin-up time** (advanced)<br>`physics.tauMs` | How fast the motors reach a new speed; lower feels snappier. | 15 ms (drone preset) | 8–80 ms | per drone |  |
| **Air drag** (advanced)<br>`physics.dragScale` | Scales the air drag of the frame: more drag slows the drone down sooner. | 1× | 0.5–2× | per drone |  |
| **Duct drag** (advanced)<br>`physics.ductDrag` | Rotor and duct drag that damps a cinewhoop's speed and wobble. | 0.6 1/s (drone preset) | 0–1.5 1/s | per drone |  |
| **Propeller inertia** (advanced)<br>`physics.propInertia` | Scales the spin inertia of the props: more inertia softens throttle and turns. | 1× | 0–3× | per drone |  |
| **Prop wash** (advanced)<br>`physics.propWash` | How much thrust the drone loses, and how much it shakes, while it sinks into its own downwash (catching a dive or a fast drop). 1 = the preset, 0 = off. The whoops have no prop wash in the simulator. | 1× | 0–2× | per drone |  |
| **Motor idle** (advanced)<br>`physics.idlePct` | Motor speed at zero throttle, like Betaflight's DShot idle value. | 10 % (drone preset) | 0–15 % | per drone |  |
| **Wind**<br>`wind.mode` | Moving air, as outdoors: it pushes the drone and carries it along, blows harder higher above the ground, and comes in gusts. The scan's wind is the one its author or the admin set for the place; live is the real wind there right now (scans with a known location); custom is your own wind for this scan. | The scan's wind | Off (still air) · The scan's wind · Live at the place · Custom | global |  |
| **Custom wind: from**<br>`wind.fromDeg` | Where the wind comes from, in compass degrees: 0 north, 90 east, 180 south, 270 west. On a scan without a compass heading, 0 is the direction the scan faces at the start. | 270° | 0–360° | per scene |  |
| **Custom wind: speed**<br>`wind.speed` | Mean speed 10 m above the ground, as a weather forecast gives it. Near the ground it is weaker, higher up stronger. A small whoop already struggles at 8-10 m/s. | 4 m/s | 0–30 m/s | per scene |  |
| **Custom wind: gusts**<br>`wind.gust` | How far the wind rises and drops around its mean speed. Gusts come and go over a few seconds; 0 is a steady wind. | 2 m/s | 0–20 m/s | per scene |  |

| Setting | What it does | Default | Range or options | Scope | Key |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| **Next scene after a crash**<br>`scenes.autoSwitch` | On: after a crash the next scene loads instead of a respawn, and you start on its platform. The radio stays connected. | Off |  | global |  |
| **Scenes to rotate through**<br>`scenes.rotation` | Where N (next scene) and the next scene after a crash come from. Shift+N is always a random scene from the author's list; F is your next favourite. | The author's list | The author's list · My favourites · Scenes I have flown | global |  |
| **Order**<br>`scenes.order` | Random: every scene once before any comes again, never the one you are in. In order: one after another, round and round. | Random | Random · In order | global |  |
| **Include scenes without walls**<br>`scenes.allowNoWalls` | Scenes without walls have no crashes: you fly through everything. Off: the rotation skips them. | Off |  | global |  |
| **Scene size**<br>`scene.transform` | Some scans are not in true metres, so the drone feels too big or too small. Or make a room huge and fly it like a mosquito, a chair as big as a house. From x0.25 to x100, around the drone; [ and ] change it in flight, x1.1 a press, with Shift x2. Kept for each scan. | 1× | 0.25×–100× | per scene | `[` `Shift+[` `]` `Shift+]` |

## Walls and voxel grid

| Setting | What it does | Default | Range or options | Scope | Key |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| **Walls (collisions)**<br>`scene.walls` | Off: the drone flies through everything, no crashes. One choice for every scan: switched off here, the walls stay off on the next scan too. Until you switch them, each scan starts as its author set it (a noisy scan may start with the walls off). C switches it. | On (per scan, set by its author) | On · Off | global | `C` |
| **Drop floating pieces under N blocks**<br>`scene.dropFloaters` | Noisy scans have floating specks that become invisible walls the drone crashes into. Every piece of the walls smaller than this many blocks (a block is 4×4×4 voxels) is removed, for this scan only. 0 keeps everything; the voxel grid shows what is left. | 0 blocks (per scan, set by its author) | 0–64 blocks | per scene |  |
| **Ignore collisions above**<br>`scene.ceiling` | Outdoor scans often have specks floating in the sky that turn into invisible walls. Above this height nothing counts as a wall. The scan's height is the one its admin set; custom is yours, set in a panel that shows it on the scan. | The scan's height | The scan's height · Off · Custom height | per scene |  |
| **Custom ceiling: height in scan metres** (advanced)<br>`scene.ceilingM` | The height in the scan's own coordinates, before Scene size: what "Show and set the height" stores for you. 10000 ignores nothing. | 10000 m (per scan, set by its author) | -10000–10000 m | per scene |  |
| **Voxel grid**<br>`voxels.show` | Shows the walls as voxels: over the scan, or instead of it (the scan hidden, you fly on the voxels). V switches it; a reload shows the scan again. | Off | Off · Over the scan · Voxels only | global | `V` |
| **Voxel style**<br>`voxels.style` | How the voxels are drawn. Floating pieces of the walls stand out in every style; "Floaters in red" colours only them. | Wireframe | Solid cubes · Wireframe · Height colours · Floaters in red | global |  |
| **Voxel opacity over the scan**<br>`voxels.opacity` | How solid the voxels look while the scan shows under them. | 0.55 | 0.05–1 | global |  |
| **Voxel opacity, voxels only**<br>`voxels.opacityOnly` | How solid the voxels look with the scan hidden. | 1 | 0.05–1 | global |  |

|---|---|---|---|---|---|

## Keyboard shortcuts

The simulator shows each key next to its menu item.

| Key | Action |
|---|---|
| `Esc` `P` | Pause / resume |
| `R` | Back to the start |
| `Y` | Rewind 5 s |
| `Enter` | Keep the wreck (no automatic respawn) |
| `N` | Next scene |
| `Shift+N` | Random scene |
| `F` | Next favourite scene |
| `M` | Flight mode |
| `Space` | Arm / disarm (keyboard flying) |
| `V` | Voxel grid: off / over the scan / voxels only |
| `C` | Walls on / off for this scan |
| `H` | Show or hide the HUD |
| `[` `Shift+[` | Scene smaller |
| `]` `Shift+]` | Scene larger |
| `F9` | Start or stop recording |
| `F3` | Frame times and delay |
| `O` | Settings |
| `B` | Report a bug or an idea |
| `L` | Share this scene |
| `K` | Keyboard keys (show / hide) |

### Keyboard flying

No radio? These keys are the sticks.

| Key | Action |
|---|---|
| `W` `S` | forward / back |
| `A` `D` | left / right |
| `←` `→` `Q` `E` | turn left / right |
| `↑` `↓` | up / down (with altitude help; without it, the throttle, which stays where you leave it) |
| `Shift` | hold: faster |
| `Space` | tap: motors on; hold half a second: motors off (easy play; pilot keys: arm / disarm) |
| `M` | self-levelling (ANGLE) or ACRO |

## Questions people ask

**Can I turn off crashes in a browser FPV simulator?**
Yes. Switch **Crashes** off in Settings and a wall hit never ends the flight, so a beginner can keep flying.

**Does it have angle / self-level mode?**
Yes: Acro (rate mode), Angle (self-levelling) or Horizon (levels, flips allowed). The default is Angle (self-levelling); the HUD chip and the M key switch it.

**Does the drone respawn by itself after a crash?**
Yes: 2 s after a crash it is back in the air, 5 s before the crash, on an invisible platform. Both times are settings (0.5–10 s and 1–30 s).

**Can I change the FPV camera angle and field of view?**
Yes, for each drone separately: camera uptilt 0–50° and field of view 70–150° (20° and 115° on the default drone).

**Can I fly an FPV drone on the Moon or Mars?**
Yes: gravity is a setting (0–30 m/s²): Earth 9.81, Moon 1.62, Mars 3.72, zero-g or anything in between. **Thrust on other worlds** picks how the motors cope: Real (same motors), Keep thrust / weight or Auto throttle (stick centre hovers).

**Can I use my own Betaflight rates and PID in the simulator?**
Yes: edit the rates in Settings (Betaflight, Raceflight, KISS, Actual or Quick curves, under Betaflight Configurator's names, with a live chart and Copy as CLI back to your quad) or paste `diff` or `diff all` from the Betaflight CLI. The rates, the PID and the throttle curve are set for the drone you fly; every drone keeps its own.

**Can I choose which radio channel arms the drone or switches the flight mode?**
Yes: Controls, then Switches. Arm, Angle / Horizon / Acro and functions such as rewind and record go on any channel from CH5 to CH16, with ranges as in Betaflight's Modes tab. Flip a switch to assign it, or paste a Betaflight `diff all` to take its aux lines.

**How hard can I hit a wall before it counts as a crash?**
That is the **Crash threshold**: 2–10 m/s for each drone, 4 m/s by default. Slower touches slide along the wall.

**Can I fix a scan that has the wrong size?**
Yes: **Scene size** scales the scan around the drone (0.25×–100×) and is remembered for each scan.

**Can I see the collision walls of a Gaussian Splatting scan?**
Yes: the **Voxel grid** shows the voxels you crash into, over the scan or voxels only.

**Can I record 60 fps video of my flight?**
Yes: **Frame rate** is 30 fps or 60 fps, 60 fps by default.

**Can I fly a 5-inch freestyle quad, a 5-inch race quad or a heavy cinelifter with a cinema camera?**
Yes: besides the BetaFPV-class whoops, **Drone** offers an iFlight Nazgul Evoque F5 class 5-inch freestyle quad, an iFlight Mach R5 Sport class 5-inch race quad and an iFlight Taurus X8 class cinelifter carrying a RED Komodo, all on 6S. Each has its own weight, thrust-to-weight, inertia, motor lag, battery and rates, and every number says where it comes from (the drone presets below).

**Does the simulator have prop wash?**
Yes, on the 5-inch quads and the cinelifter: sinking into its own downwash (catching a dive or a fast drop) the drone loses thrust and shakes. **Prop wash** scales it for each drone (0–2×; 0 switches it off).

**Can I help make a simulator drone fly like my real one, or ask for a new drone?**
Yes. The presets are built from published numbers and estimates. If you fly one of them for real and it feels different, press **Help tune it** in the drone picker or under Drone in Settings (or open `/en/fly/?drone=<id>&open=tune`) and send your Betaflight `diff all`, a link to a blackbox log and a few words; Andrii fits the drone to it. The same form asks for a drone that is not in the list. How every number was made: [docs/research/drones-v08.md](https://github.com/AndriiShramko/ShramkoGSFPV/blob/main/docs/research/drones-v08.md).
